extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities, small-business representatives, practitioners and members of the public who read or submit comments on SEC rulemaking (notice-and-comment participants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required content for the Securities and Exchange Commission's semiannual Regulatory Flexibility Agenda entries and the public notice-and-comment process for items listed therein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) agenda requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The RFA requires each Federal agency, twice each year, to publish in the Federal Register an agenda identifying rules that the agency expects to consider in the next 12 months that are likely to have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities (5 U.S.C. 602(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of the agenda does not preclude an agency from considering or acting on any matter not included, and an agency is not required to consider or act on any matter that is included (5 U.S.C. 602(d)). Actions without estimated dates are placed in the long-term category but may nevertheless be acted on within the next 12 months. The Commission prints only those agenda entries for which preparation of an RFA analysis is required. The Commission's complete RFA agenda will be available online at www.reginfo.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment submission requirements and cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be submitted by the stated deadline (e.g., 'Comments should be received on or before July 24, 2019').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods: use the Commission's internet comment form or send email to rule-comments@sec.gov, or send paper comments to the SEC Secretary at the listed address. Include the File Number (e.g., S7-04-19) on the subject line. To help processing, use only one submission method. The Commission will post all comments on its website and 'all comments received will be posted without change.' Persons submitting comments are cautioned that the Commission does not redact or edit personal identifying information; 'You should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of official PDF / verification against official edition
rubrics_metrics.description: The XML rendition on FederalRegister.gov is informational and not the official legal edition; 'This document has been published in the Federal Register. Use the PDF linked in the document sidebar for the official electronic format.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While efforts are made to ensure accurate display, those relying on the site for legal research should verify results against an official edition of the Federal Register (govinfo.gov). Until ACFR grants official status, the XML rendition 'does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts.' Only official editions provide legal notice of publication under 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document heading elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Document headings vary by document type but may contain the following elements:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements include: the agency or agencies that issued and signed the document; the number of the CFR title and the number of each part the document amends, proposes to amend, or is directly related to; the agency docket number / agency internal file number; the RIN which identifies each regulatory action listed in the Unified Agenda. See the Document Drafting Handbook for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda entry content and required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agenda entry includes standardized fields that describe the rulemaking action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical fields shown in the entries: Sequence No.; Title; Regulation Identifier No.; Designation (e.g., Independent agency); Legal Authority; Abstract; Timetable (Action names and Dates, FR Cite); 'Regulatory Flexibility Analysis Required' flag; Agency Contact (name, division, address, phone, email); RIN. Entries may also show status categories (Proposed Rule Stage, Final Rule Stage, Long-Term Actions, Completed Actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable action types and dating conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agenda timetables list action types and associated dates (when known).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common action entries include: NPRM, NPRM Comment Period End, Final Action, Interim Final Rule, Interim Final Rule Effective, Next Action Undetermined, Second NPRM, Final Action Effective, etc. Dates may be exact, listed with FR citation (e.g., '07/14/15 80 FR 41144'), or 'To Be Determined' / 'Undetermined' when not yet set. Actions placed in 'long-term' may nevertheless be acted on within 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Analysis flag
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Regulatory Flexibility Analysis Required:' indicates whether an RFA analysis is required for the listed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agenda explicitly prints those entries for which preparation of an RFA analysis is required and marks the field 'Yes' or 'No' as appropriate for each action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency contact information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agenda entry provides a named agency contact with office, postal address, phone, and email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format: Name, Division, Securities and Exchange Commission, Street address, Phone: [number], Email: [address]. This contact is the person to reach for further information about the entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard statutory abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: The agenda lists and uses standard abbreviations for statutes administered by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: 'Securities Act'—Securities Act of 1933; 'Exchange Act'—Securities Exchange Act of 1934; 'Investment Company Act'—Investment Company Act of 1940; 'Investment Advisers Act'—Investment Advisers Act of 1940; 'Dodd Frank Act'—Jumpstart Our Business Startups Act; 'JOBS Act'—Jumpstart Our Business Startups Act; 'FAST Act'—Fixing America's Surface Transportation Act. (The page provides a set of the abbreviations used in the agenda.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and alternative formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Document-related metrics and multiple machine-readable formats are provided for public use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page indicates 'Document page views' statistics and lists 'Other Formats' available such as JSON (normalized attributes and metadata), XML (original full text XML), and MODS (GPO metadata). It points to developer tools pages for more information and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of contents and navigation disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: The enhanced table of contents is a navigational aid processed from headings within legal text and has no substantive legal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes that repetition of headings to form internal navigation links 'has no substantive legal effect.' It is presented as a convenience for readers, not a legal element of the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection and research verification caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Public inspection PDFs are available, but users are advised to verify contents against the official Federal Register when using them for legal research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states: 'If you are using public inspection listings for legal research, you should verify the contents of the documents against a final, official edition of the Federal Register.' It reiterates that only official editions provide legal and judicial notice under 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507.
